question: Starting only with the supplied website, find other websites with source-backed technical connections during the specified historical window. Choose and justify your own pivots. Keep capture dates and exact tracking identifiers separate; do not infer identity, ownership, control or motives.
input_policy: This file is the investigation input. Do not read the five-capture replay task, its oracle or measured results, published case conclusions, case screenshots, or feasibility notes as a source of comparison domains. Public reporting and search snippets are not independent verification.
collection_policy: Use bounded public-source collection. Inspect archive listings before selecting a dated capture. Do not purchase data or consume paid API credits without separate approval.
discovery_policy: An exact literal in the seed can justify a reverse-index query, not a new domain guessed from memory. Retain the actual reverse-index response, identifier match, historical observation dates and provenance. Index associations are third-party leads, not ownership evidence. Independently inspect a dated capture of any discovered comparison site before claiming a shared technical observation.
pass_requirements: At least one additional website was reached through a retained, citable discovery lead rather than supplied as a seed or remembered from reporting.
Independent retained historical HTML supports the exact shared technical identifier with valid original-byte spans; full UA properties remain distinct.
The graph presents only source-attributed observations and exposes dates and original evidence.
Every analytical finding remains pending until local human review; no identity or ownership conclusion is approved automatically.
stop_policy: If an accessible historical index, permission, credits, evidence or collection budget is missing, stop and record discovery_blocked. Successful extraction, an intact case or an empty search is not a discovery pass. Describe the missing capability precisely.
